summary: Saubhagya Pradhananga is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Attested in 2018, Pradhananga served as Chief of the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Saurabh Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of Delhi, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, and Deccan College, and held positions at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and the University of Delhi.
Saverio Sani is an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the University of Genoa from circa 1987 to 1998 and at the University of Pisa (attested 1996–1998).

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist studies scholar and teacher who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Nandasiri Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda (1927–2005) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under U Paññāvanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. He taught at the University of Mandalay, led several monasteries, and served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.

Sayadaw U Thittila (1896–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. He served as a librarian for the Adyar Library and the Buddhist Society, and later lectured at the University of Rangoon.
Sayagyi U Ba Khin (1899–1971) was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied under Saya Thetgyi and founded the International Meditation Centre.

Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under Shinobu Yamaguchi and Shogo Watanabe, later serving as a visiting researcher there and working at the Cabinet Office in 2020.
Sayori Tsubota works in Indology. She pursued a PhD at Osaka University (attested 2020) and held a post at Tohoku University (attested 2026).
Scarlett J. He is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She has studied as a PhD student and held a post at Columbia University.

Schuyler Cammann (1912–1991) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kent School, Yale, Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and under Helmut Hoffmann, and served on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1983.

Scott A. Mitchell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne and has served as a professor and president at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Scott DeLancey is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied under Yungdrung Manang. He joined the faculty of the University of Oregon circa 1982.

Scott Hurley is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison, earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, and became an associate professor at Luther College in 2002.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the Australian National University. He has held positions at ANU, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski—having also studied under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg—and held a post there.

Sebastian Nehrdich works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the Universities of Hamburg, Kyoto, and Düsseldorf, he has held posts at Hamburg, Düsseldorf, UC Berkeley, and Tohoku University.
Sebastian Pole is a scholar in Indology. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado (1855–1922) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Pontifical Institute of Saint Apollinaris. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Curso Superior de Letras and later at the University of Lisbon.
See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).
